source_heading: A-RC01 — Separate city attribution from household context
source_claim: A Nippur city attribution does not, without further evidence, establish a particular house, archive or resident group.
reason: Source-handling rule: city attribution and household context must be separated; retained in QA rather than as a historical proposition.

source_heading: A-RC02 — Preserve inferred dating and identification
source_claim: The proposed date and archive connection of UM 29-16-672 must remain qualified rather than be treated as a preserved date formula and secure archive label.
reason: Date and archive affiliation are explicitly inferential; insufficient for a stable local proposition without further verification.

source_heading: A-RC03 — Retain bounded positive visibility
source_claim: BE 6/2, 23 attests the participation identified in TX03; the observation does not establish a citywide rate or universal inheritance arrangement.
reason: Positive attestation of Narubtum and the inheritance episode is preserved in the consolidated estate-allocation proposition.

source_heading: A-RC04 — Do not count the model text as an act
source_claim: P368911 is identified as didactic; its contract-like content is not itself proof that the depicted transaction occurred.
reason: Merged with an independent Nippur school witness into the genre/event distinction.

source_heading: A-RC05 — Exclude placeholder seal links from historical identification
source_claim: The P533185/S999999 link does not supply a shared historical seal owner for the inspected objects.
reason: Modern catalogue placeholder behavior is a source-control rule, not an ancient historical proposition.

source_heading: A-RC06 — Keep late activity distinct from neighborhood continuity
source_claim: The late evidence discussed in LC01 prevents treating one early documentary cessation as a demonstrated end to every kind of Nippur activity.
reason: Retained as a qualified late-chronology synthesis based on specialist reanalysis.

source_heading: A-RC07 — Retain disputed market provenance
source_claim: The four attributions identified in LC02 must not be cited as uncontested excavated origins.
reason: Market-tablet provenance is explicitly disputed; no contested attribution is promoted as local fact.

source_heading: A-RC08 — No demographic denominator from this return
source_claim: The present purposive sample does not support citywide household frequencies, average household size or population shares.
reason: Research-coverage/denominator rule; retained in QA as a prohibition on demographic extrapolation.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — Marriage contribution and differentiated consequences
source_claim: BE 6/2 40 records a woman’s nineteen-shekel marriage contribution and different treatment of that contribution under husband- versus wife-initiated repudiation.
reason: Primary formulation of the BE 6/2, 40 contribution/repudiation proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — Parenthood constituted alongside marriage
source_claim: BE 6/2 48 makes Naramtum a legally recognized mother to Awiliya’s three sons and connects recognition/support to estate rights.
reason: Constituted motherhood/support/estate terms retained; conditional breach clause also preserved.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — Continuing sibling maintenance duty
source_claim: PBS 8/2 116 places maintenance duties toward Bēltani on four named brothers/heirs, with consequences for inheritance upon default.
reason: Merged with title, alienation restriction, and witness evidence from the same agreement.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — A woman as a named witness
source_claim: Unnubtum, a nadītu of Ninurta, is a witness in PBS 8/2 116.
reason: Distinct witness role preserved inside the consolidated single-document proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — Marriage and pre-existing children
source_claim: SAOC 44 1 combines marriage with affiliation of the wife’s three children; its identification as a widow’s remarriage is supported by Stol’s discussion of the equivalent MC 3 14.
reason: Retained with widow-remarriage interpretation explicitly downgraded to mediated scholarship.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — Property division is not automatically household division
source_claim: SAOC 44 44/46/47 records joint house-property acquisition followed by purchase of the other partner’s share.
reason: Merged with the broader House I legal/property sequence; residential inference remains excluded.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — Residence and property participation are different associations
source_claim: The examined TA records distinguish an expressly reported resident, contributors to an acquisition and a tenant’s temporary house access.
reason: Represented in the explicit-residence versus other housing associations proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — Legal release without a demonstrated residential exit
source_claim: SAOC 44 53 records manumission; the consulted catalogue does not specify the released person’s subsequent residence.
reason: Merged with the text-level temporal service/status distinction; absence of residential exit remains a limit.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — Heirship and lifetime provision could be linked
source_claim: Some inspected adoption instruments combine heirship/property arrangements with obligations to provide support during the adopter’s lifetime. Local claim: C-C01.
reason: Two independent adoption documents preserved as a cross-case support/heirship proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — A female adopter’s assets had a prior gift history
source_claim: Narāmtum, explicitly designated nadītu/lukur of Lugal-aba, adopted Ur-Pabilsaga using assets attributed to a gift from her father. Local claim: C-C02.
reason: Retained as a specific Narāmtum property-history/adoption proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — Mannum’s inheritance chronology must use the revised date
source_claim: The published re-edition of MC 3, 51 dates the partition to Samsu-iluna 10, not the older year 23; an argument excluding inheritance because it occurred too late must therefore be reconsidered. Local claims: C-C06–C-C07.
reason: Retained as a source-critical chronological correction with wider reconstruction kept moderate.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — Prior gifts could constrain later estate settlements
source_claim: A lifetime gift to Nanna-meša’s daughter Nin-kuzu was acknowledged in a later settlement involving other family claimants, compensation and waiver. Local claim: C-C09.
reason: Retained as a prior-gift/later-settlement proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — Inherited resources could change form through exchange
source_claim: Mannum exchanged inherited and preferential built-property rights for fractions of recurring institutional rights. Local claim: C-C11.
reason: Retained as a specific exchange of built-property rights for institutional rights.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — Earlier expense claims could affect later heirs
source_claim: A settlement recognized Mannum’s earlier expenses for Ibbī-Enlil and transferred an institutional entitlement from the heirs. Local claim: C-C12.
reason: Retained as a specific expense-claim/heir settlement proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — An earlier adoption remained consequential in a later division
source_claim: Narāmtum’s adoption of Ur-Pabilsaga was invoked in a later estate division between him and Narubtum; the later instrument records separate allocations, including enslaved persons. Local claims: C-C15–C-C16.
reason: Longitudinal adoption-to-later-division link retained; same BE 6/2, 23 act is not double-counted.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — Heirship could be terminated with future claims excluded
source_claim: Judges directed termination of Ilī-u-Šamaš’s heirship and a no-claim instrument extending exclusion to his heirs. Local claims: C-C18–C-C19.
reason: Retained as a specific judicial termination/no-claim proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 9 — Legal continuity is not itself evidence of continuous residence
source_claim: The two reconstructed dossiers establish successive relationships, claims and reallocations without independently establishing an unchanged co-resident group. Local claims: C-C20–C-C22.
reason: Merged with provenance controls showing that legal continuity does not independently prove co-residence.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — Distinguishable claims within family-linked resources (D-C01)
source_claim: Named family participants can hold different claims in resources; a household label does not specify those rights.
reason: Retained as a bounded cross-case rights proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — Partition followed by share consolidation (D-C03)
source_claim: A documented house partition was followed rapidly by three share purchases by one coheir.
reason: Retained as the dated partition-to-consolidation sequence.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — Heterogeneous inheritance portfolios (D-C05)
source_claim: Division could distribute heterogeneous assets, including land, movable goods, resource entitlements, and enslaved persons, with balancing transfers.
reason: Merged with BE 6/2, 23/26 estate-allocation evidence, including named enslaved persons.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — Transfer of annual office entitlements (D-C06)
source_claim: Specified annual portions of temple-office entitlements could enter exchanges and inheritance divisions.
reason: Merged with additional independent time-defined and transferable office-right witnesses.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — Marriage contribution and contingent restitution (D-C08)
source_claim: A marriage agreement separately identifies the wife’s silver contribution and conditional return/forfeiture obligations.
reason: Substantively duplicates B-RC01 on the same BE 6/2, 40 clauses; no independent corroborative weight added.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — Maintenance attached to inheritance eligibility (D-C09)
source_claim: Family maintenance obligations could be explicitly attached to continuing inheritance entitlement.
reason: Cross-case synthesis adds no distinct predicate after BE 6/2, 48 and PBS 8/2, 116 are separately preserved.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — Agreement-specific restriction on field alienation (D-C10)
source_claim: One support agreement restricts heirs’ alienation of fields during the beneficiary’s lifetime.
reason: Agreement-specific alienation restriction is preserved inside the consolidated PBS 8/2, 116 proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — Different stated interest terms (D-C11)
source_claim: The selected loan texts distinguish stated interest-bearing obligations from a text marked not bearing interest.
reason: Retained as an explicit cross-text interest-status contrast.

source_heading: Candidate 9 — Different advance and settlement media (D-C12)
source_claim: An obligation could link different commodities or media at advance and settlement.
reason: Retained, with PBS 8/2, 130 as the secure core and uncertain-provenance supplement demoted.

source_heading: Candidate 10 — Cultivation and annual yield-share rent (D-C14)
source_claim: Cultivation and an annually assessed yield-share claim could be allocated through a lease rather than a permanent land sale.
reason: Primary formulation of the BE 6/2, 29 cultivation lease proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 11 — Recorded adjudication and property settlement (D-C16)
source_claim: A legal record narrates adjudication and an executed property settlement concerning earlier family transactions.
reason: Merged with G’s authority-interface reading; old-edition terminology remains a caveat.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — E-C01: Hire mediated through a father
source_claim: BE 6/2 51 records Idin-Ištar, explicitly the son of Nabi-Šamaš, hired from Nabi-Šamaš by Lu-Ninsianna for a fixed term with a monthly grain payment.
reason: Retained as the father-mediated fixed-term hire proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — E-C02: Kinship and maintenance obligations
source_claim: Nippur agreements connect filial or adoptive relationships with inheritance-linked maintenance obligations; these are not identical to ownership of the obligated person.
reason: General synthesis is fully represented by the two specific BE 6/2, 48 and BE 6/2, 28 propositions.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — E-C03: Enslaved people in estate allocation
source_claim: BE 6/2 23 allocates four named enslaved people between the shares of Narubtum and Ur-Pabilsaĝa.
reason: Same BE 6/2, 23 allocation is already preserved in the consolidated estate-allocation proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — E-C04: Conditional enslavement is not an accomplished sale
source_claim: BE 6/2 24 stipulates sale following adoptees’ repudiation of their adoptive parents; the clause does not report that repudiation or sale occurred.
reason: Retained because it distinguishes prospective sanction from realized event.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — E-C05: Paid manumission with qualified Nippur attribution
source_claim: BE 6/2 8 records Ištar-rabiat’s manumission, a payment of ten shekels to Duššubtum, and protection against named heirs’ future claims; its Nippur attribution requires a provenance qualification.
reason: Retained with explicit provenance qualification and MODERATE confidence.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — E-C06: Institutional livelihood rights in family property
source_claim: BE 6/2 43 places a six-month annual Enlil priestly office share and associated livelihood land within a family property division.
reason: Merged into the family-patrimony proposition centered on BE 6/2, 43.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — E-C07: Cultivation through a lease, not a personal hire
source_claim: BE 6/2 29 records Damu-idinnam’s lease of Ibgatum’s field for cultivation at one-third of returns as annual rent.
reason: Substantively duplicates D-RC10 on BE 6/2, 29; no independent weight added.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — E-C08: Marital breach clauses vary
source_claim: BE 6/2 48 and 40 prescribe different consequences for a wife’s repudiation: the former includes sale, while the latter specifies financial consequences.
reason: The cross-document contrast is preserved by the two underlying marriage propositions; no separate general rule is needed.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — F-C01: Transferable interests without an identified resident census
source_claim: The six catalogued House I contracts record changing rights in house property through partition, sale, exchange, and transfer of a partner’s share; they do not establish a complete co-resident group.
reason: Merged with B’s overlapping legal sequence while retaining the broader six-contract and context caveats.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — F-C02/F-C03: One final deposit is not successive named occupations
source_claim: The House I transaction sequence is associated with a final XA-1 assemblage; it does not provide six separately documented occupation phases.
reason: Retained as a separate depositional/occupation-phase proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — F-C07/F-C09: Instructional activity does not identify the household
source_claim: TA House F’s earlier assemblage strongly supports instructional activity; its later legal texts do not establish the identity or household composition of the earlier teaching occupants.
reason: Retained with confidence split between instructional activity and cross-phase identity limit.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — F-C13/F-C14: Atta’s cache associates a person with a place, not title to it
source_claim: The cache in TB House O links a substantial temple-office dossier to Atta and to a specific deposit; the dossier does not establish ownership of the excavated building.
reason: Retained as archive-person-place association without ownership inference.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — F-C10/F-C15: Document biographies can outlast transactions
source_claim: Later deposits at Nippur include older legal records and, in a linked office sequence, records of a prior holder’s acquisition; the date and parties of a deed cannot automatically date or identify the deposit’s resident group.
reason: Retained as a document-biography/deposit chronology proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — F-C12: Physical subdivision need not disclose its legal cause
source_claim: TB House C’s published subdivision supports a change in spatial organization without establishing a corresponding named family partition.
reason: Retained with no named legal/family cause inferred.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — F-C06/F-C20: Legal relationships need not carry an archaeological address
source_claim: A house lease and sequential estate partitions identify legal relationships without necessarily identifying the parties’ excavated residence.
reason: Merged into the broader legal-continuity/address evidentiary boundary.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — Recurring annual terms (G-C01)
source_claim: Some Nippur temple-linked rights were specified as recurring periods within a year, rather than undifferentiated full-time offices.
reason: Recurring annual terms preserved within the broader time-defined transferable-rights proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — Sale and exchange of institutional rights (G-C02)
source_claim: The selected Nippur corpus attests both sale and exchange of temple-office rights.
reason: Sale/exchange evidence preserved in the same consolidated office-right proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — Family patrimony with differentiated assets (G-C03)
source_claim: Office-linked rights could form part of family patrimony alongside other assets, without all family property necessarily merging.
reason: Retained as family patrimony with differentiated office-linked assets.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — Paternal-house recovery (G-C05)
source_claim: Some Nippur reacquisitions explicitly characterize the recovered resource as belonging to the paternal house.
reason: Merged with the titled-women case while preserving legal-mechanism uncertainty.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — Adoption and protected office/property claims (G-C06)
source_claim: A Nippur adoption deed protects specified office/property rights of the adoptee against claims by the named adoptive brother.
reason: Retained as a specific adoption/protected-rights proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — Titled women and family land (G-C07)
source_claim: A woman bearing a Ninurta-related religious title is documented recovering paternal-house land from another similarly titled woman.
reason: Specific titled-women instance preserved inside paternal-house recovery proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — Family claims through multiple authorities (G-C08)
source_claim: One Ninlil-related family dispute records royal referral to Nippur’s council followed by a house/property settlement.
reason: Merged with D’s adjudication/settlement reading of the same ancient record.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — Deeds, death and future-claim liability (G-C09)
source_claim: Receipt of deeds for an office and inheritance after a former holder’s death carried explicit responsibility for future claims.
reason: Retained as a distinct deed-custody/future-claim liability proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 1 — A measured house property is not a household roster
source_claim: Measured é properties are not descriptions of complete residential groups. (H-C01)
reason: Retained as the direct measured-property/roster distinction.

source_heading: Candidate 2 — Explicit residence is a distinct statement
source_claim: Residence can be stated explicitly rather than inferred from an é–person association. (H-C02)
reason: Retained as the strongest direct positive residence wording in the package.

source_heading: Candidate 3 — Living allocation and conditional heirship
source_claim: A living father’s division can be combined with conditional heirship and annual support. (H-C04)
reason: Retained as the BE 6/2, 28 allocation/heirship/support proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 4 — Kinship, cult title and support entitlement
source_claim: A woman’s kinship and deity-linked title can be stated together with a maintenance entitlement. (H-C07)
reason: Merged with the same agreement’s sibling support, field restriction, and witness role.

source_heading: Candidate 5 — Annual dues are not inherently wages
source_claim: Annual payment terminology is not confined to remuneration for labor. (H-C09)
reason: Retained as a bounded lexical/obligation distinction across rent and support contexts.

source_heading: Candidate 6 — Release and continuing service require temporal analysis
source_claim: A manumission-related instrument distinguishes lifetime service from heirs’ later slave-status claims. (H-C11)
reason: Merged with B’s no-residential-exit caution and the same damaged manumission-related instrument.

source_heading: Candidate 7 — ARAD names and devotional formulas do not establish slavery
source_claim: ARAD in a divine seal formula or personal name is insufficient evidence of a person’s slave status. (H-C12)
reason: Retained as a semantic/status caution grounded in two specific textual environments.

source_heading: Candidate 8 — Transferable temple rights can be time-defined
source_claim: Temple-linked rights could be described in temporal portions and transferred. (H-C13)
reason: Adds independent SAOC witnesses to the broader time-defined transferable office-right proposition.

source_heading: Candidate 9 — Mixed writing is not evidence of a speaker’s vernacular
source_claim: A single instrument can combine Akkadian syntax/verbs with Sumerian-written legal expressions. (H-C16)
reason: Retained as a direct writing/vernacular evidentiary distinction.

source_heading: Candidate 10 — A didactic legal witness is not an event register
source_claim: A Nippur school witness can attest legal vocabulary without certifying a contemporary legal event. (H-C17)
reason: Independent didactic witness merged with A’s model-text case; not double-counted as an event.
